pull_requests.author: connor4312
pull_requests.body: chat: back terminal chat with the Agent HostAdds an experimental path that backs Terminal Chat with an Agent Host session instead of theextension host. Sessions created for throwaway UI surfaces are marked ephemeral so they arenever retained or listed, and the terminal surface supplies per-turn instructions that keepanswers focused on a single command.- Adds `chat.terminal.agentHost.enabled` (default off, startup experiment) to select the  backend. When disabled, session creation follows the previous extension-host path exactly.- Adds `TerminalChatSessionResolver`, which applies the Agent Host preference, falls back to a  local session when the Agent Host is unavailable or fails, and reports the contribution the  widget must lock to. Requests then carry `agentIdSilent`, because a contributed session type  is not the default agent for its location.- Adds an optional `locations` to chat session contributions, which defaults to the primary  Chat surface, so a session type can serve the terminal.- Adds the `vscode.chat.ephemeralSession` metadata slot. The Agent Host tombstones such  sessions at creation, omits them from the session list and the overlay summaries, and  collects them after their last subscription ends.- Adds the `vscode.chat.surface` metadata slot, which carries the shell type and the operating  system. `AgentSideEffects` uses it to add terminal instructions to each turn. The widget  refreshes the slot when the shell type becomes known.- Replaces `AgentSessionRegistry.unregister` with `tombstone`, because the two methods did the  same operation.- Shows the widget immediately and waits for the session only before a request is sent, so the  Agent Host round trip does not delay the terminal chat display.(Commit message generated by Copilot)

pull_requests.title: Select-to-line-start jumps to end of previous line when before an indented token
pull_requests.author: srikanthananthula63053
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #331582

## Problem

When the cursor sits right before an indented token on a line — i.e. right after the leading whitespace/tabs and before the first real character — pressing `Cmd+Shift+Left` (macOS) / `Ctrl+Shift+Home`'s sibling `Shift+Home` (`cursorHomeSelect`) selects backwards across that line's own indentation to column 1, instead of doing anything useful with the previous line:

```ts
const memberships = await this.entityManager.find(
    |CompanyMembershipEntity,
```

Press `Cmd+Shift+Left` once → selection spans only the leading spaces on the *same* line:

```ts
|    CompanyMembershipEntity,
```

Pulling `CompanyMembershipEntity` up onto the `find(` line then requires pressing Backspace once per indentation character/tab-stop, rather than once.

## Root cause

`cursorHomeSelect` and plain `cursorHome` both call the same "smart home" toggle in `MoveOperations.moveToBeginningOfLine` (`src/vs/editor/common/cursor/cursorMoveOperations.ts`):

- if the cursor isn't yet at the line's first non-whitespace column, move there;
- if it's already there, move to true column 1 of the *same* line.

That second stage never looks outside the current line, so when the cursor is already positioned right before the content (immediately after the indentation), the only thing left to select on that line is the indentation itself — which isn't useful on its own, since a single Backspace from column 1 already joins the line with the previous one and keeps the indentation as-is.

## Fix

In `MoveOperations.moveToBeginningOfLine`, when selecting (`inSelectionMode`) and the cursor is already at the first non-whitespace column of a line that (a) actually has leading whitespace and (b) isn't the first line of the buffer, extend the selection to the end of the previous line instead of column 1 of the current line:

```ts
if (inSelectionMode && firstNonBlankColumn > minColumn && lineNumber > 1) {
    const previousLineNumber = lineNumber - 1;
    return cursor.move(inSelectionMode, previousLineNumber, model.getLineMaxColumn(previousLineNumber), 0);
}
```

A single Backspace afterwards then removes the newline and the entire indentation in one step, pulling the token onto the previous line.

Unaffected on purpose:
- Plain (non-select) `Home`/`Cmd+Left` — unchanged, still stays on the current line.
- Lines with no leading whitespace — nothing to skip, so the toggle behaves as before.
- The first line of the buffer — no previous line to jump to.
- Any selection call where the cursor isn't yet at the first non-whitespace column — unchanged, still moves there first as before.

This only touches the shared model-level move function, so it applies consistently whether reached through the plain (non-wrapped) path or the soft-wrap–aware view-line path that already delegates to it.

## Testing

Added to `src/vs/editor/test/browser/controller/cursor.test.ts`, next to the existing "move to beginning of line" tests:
- The exact repro from the issue (spaces indentation), including that a second press falls back to the normal same-line toggle once there's nothing left to skip.
- Tabs indentation.
- Previous line ending in punctuation (`{`), confirming the cursor lands immediately after it.
- Plain (non-select) Home is unaffected.
- A line with no leading whitespace is unaffected.

Validation performed:
- `scripts/test.bat --run vs/editor/test/browser/controller/cursor.test.js` — 259 passing (254 pre-existing + 5 new), 0 failing.
- `scripts/test.bat --run vs/editor/test/browser/controller/cursorMoveCommand.test.js` — 56 passing, 0 failing.
- `scripts/test.bat --run vs/editor/contrib/wordOperations/test/browser/wordOperations.test.js` — 57 passing, 0 failing.
- `npm run typecheck-client` — 0 errors.

pull_requests.title: Await Workspace Trust transition completion in setUrisTrust()
pull_requests.author: zainnadeem786
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #328625

## Summary

Ensure `WorkspaceTrustManagementService.setUrisTrust()` does not resolve until the underlying Workspace Trust transition has completed.

## Root Cause

`setUrisTrust()` invoked the asynchronous `doSetUrisTrust(...)` operation without awaiting its returned promise.

As a result, callers awaiting `setUrisTrust()` or `setWorkspaceTrust()` could resume before asynchronous Workspace Trust transition participants completed and before `onDidChangeTrust` was emitted.

## Change

Await the existing `doSetUrisTrust(...)` promise inside `setUrisTrust()`.

This ensures that the public promise resolves only after the complete Workspace Trust transition has finished.

## Regression Test

Added a focused regression test that registers a controlled asynchronous Workspace Trust transition participant and verifies that `setWorkspaceTrust()` remains unresolved until:

- the transition participant completes; and
- the `onDidChangeTrust` event fires.

The test fails on the previous implementation and passes after the fix.

## Validation

- `npm run compile`
- `.\scripts\test.bat --grep "setWorkspaceTrust waits for trust transition participants before resolving"`
  - `1 passing`
- `.\scripts\test.bat --grep "Workspace Trust"`
  - `10 passing`
- `git diff --check`

pull_requests.title: agentHost: Collect and package debug logs on the host
pull_requests.author: roblourens
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Reworks **Developer: Export Agent Host Debug Logs** so the Agent Host owns discovery and packaging of host-side diagnostics instead of the client guessing host filesystem paths.

- Adds a typed private AHP extension request, `vscode/collectAgentHostDebugLogs`, returning an opaque artifact URI.
- Uses the Copilot SDK's `session.rpc.debug.collectLogs` API for SDK-owned events, process logs, and shell logs.
- Keeps client-owned logs on the client: window/shared-process output, AHP JSONL transport logs, remote-forwarded channels, and usage/customization sidecars.
- Produces one final ZIP; native exports flatten the Agent Host archive into it.
- Supports export with or without an active session. With a session, SDK events/shell logs are included. Without one, collection remains host-wide and excludes unrelated session events/shell logs.

## Remote transfer

The artifact contract is a URI, not inline bytes.

- Local Agent Host artifacts are ordinary local `file:` URIs and never transfer archive bytes over IPC.
- Remote Agent Host artifacts are downloaded through the private `vscode/readAgentHostDebugLogsChunk` request in bounded 1 MiB chunks.
- The old whole-file Base64 read path is not used as a fallback.
- The chunk reader only serves artifacts produced and retained by the collector; it is not a general-purpose remote file read.

## Safety and lifecycle

- Bounds archive bytes, staged bytes, individual files, and archive entry count.
- Keeps the tail of oversized logs so recent failures remain diagnosable.
- Validates ZIP entry count/expanded size before flattening and rejects duplicate final paths.
- Expires abandoned host artifacts and cleans staging/artifacts on completion and shutdown.
- Validates the returned artifact URI scheme, kind, and declared sizes.
- Verifies actual streamed byte count against the declared artifact size.
- SDK/provider collection failures surface to the user instead of silently switching to a second path-guessing implementation.

## Compatibility

This intentionally uses the existing private AHP extension-method seam rather than changing the generated public protocol while the shape settles. A remote host that predates the request returns `MethodNotFound` as an explicit collection failure.

## Validation

- Client typecheck and full product/Copilot compile pass.
- Agent Host, chat browser, Agents provider, ZIP, protocol routing, and streaming tests pass.
- Layer validation and hygiene pass.
- Manually verified in Code OSS:
  - Active Copilot session ZIP includes `agenthost.log`, SDK `events.jsonl`/process logs, and client-owned logs.
  - No-active/New Session ZIP includes host/window/shared/AHP/process logs without unrelated `events.jsonl`.
  - Active Codex session produces the common host artifact without Copilot-specific entries.
  - Repeated exports leave no temporary artifacts.

(Written by Copilot)

pull_requests.title: Fix section checkbox state when all items are unchecked
pull_requests.author: srikanthananthula63053
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

The Agent Customizations migration UI (introduced in #330539 / #330772, tested in #330793) groups migration candidates (e.g. Workspace/User prompt files, or Agents/Instructions) under a section with a "select all" group checkbox. Unchecking every individual item in a group was expected to also uncheck the group checkbox, but it stayed checked.

## Root cause

`renderCustomizationMigrationPage` computes each group checkbox's initial `checked` state once, from `customizations.every(...)`, when the group is rendered. Clicking the group checkbox itself triggers a full page re-render (which recomputes this correctly), but toggling an individual item's checkbox only updated the item's own state — nothing recalculated or updated the containing group's checkbox afterward, so it kept showing whatever state it had at the last full render.

## Fix

`renderSelectionCheckbox`/`renderItem` now accept an optional `onSelectionChange` callback. `renderGroup` passes a callback that recomputes `customizations.every(...)` for that group and updates `groupCheckbox.checked` accordingly, so the group checkbox stays in sync as individual items are (un)checked — without a full page re-render.

## Tests added

Added a regression test in `aiCustomizationManagementEditor.test.ts`: `unchecking every item in a migration group unchecks the group checkbox`. It renders a group with two items, unchecks them one at a time, and asserts the group checkbox's `aria-checked` goes to `false` after the first uncheck and stays `false` after the last — then re-checking both items brings it back to `true`. Verified this test fails (group checkbox stays `true`) against the unpatched code and passes with the fix.

## Validation performed

- `npm run typecheck-client` — no errors
- `scripts\test.bat --run vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/aiCustomization/aiCustomizationManagementEditor.test.js` — 12/12 passing
- `scripts\test.bat --runGlob "**/aiCustomization*.test.js"` — full related suite, 61/61 passing
- `npx eslint` on both changed files — clean

Fixes #331330

pull_requests.title: agents window: fix sessions list progress
pull_requests.author: justschen
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Fixes Sessions list progress indicators becoming stale in either direction:

- a session is running, but the list does not show a spinner;
- a session has completed, but the list continues showing a spinner.

## Root cause

The Agent Host correctly aggregated chat activity into the session status, but did not publish the resulting session-summary updates for sessions initially returned by `root/listSessions`.

A recent publication filter only emitted `root/sessionSummaryChanged` for sessions recorded as published. That record was updated for `root/sessionAdded`, but not for `root/listSessions`. As a result, restored/listed sessions were visible to the client while the host still treated their summaries as unpublished.

The subscribed chat continued receiving live `session/chatUpdated` actions, so the chat content showed the correct state. The Sessions list depended on the suppressed root summary update and retained its previous state, producing the mismatch.

## Fix

- Record summaries returned by `root/listSessions` as published without emitting redundant `root/sessionAdded` notifications.
- Preserve the listed summary as the notification-diff baseline so subsequent status and activity changes are emitted normally.
- Keep filtered sessions unpublished, preserving the existing external-session visibility behavior.
- Remove the client-side status recomputation workaround; the UI now consumes the status published by the Agent Host.
- Add a protocol-level regression test covering a restored session returned by `listSessions` and its subsequent transition to in progress.

pull_requests.title: Render evidence chapters from the automation harness
pull_requests.author: bryanchen-d
pull_requests.body:
Follow-up to #331558 (merged), which added `VSCODE_EVIDENCE_CLEAN_CAPTURE=1`. Rebased onto `main`, so this diff now contains only the changes below.

## Summary

Moves evidence chaptering into the harness so a **clean capture can still be annotated**.

#331558 stopped the step banner being drawn into the window under test, but left nothing in its place: a local run produced an unannotated recording. This adds the annotation back as a post-processing step.

## Changes

- **`videoStartedAt` is recorded natively.** Both launchers stamp the moment the recording context is created and pass it to `PlaywrightDriver`; the evidence manifest exports it. Without an origin, captured step timestamps cannot be converted into offsets in the video.
- **`test/mcp/scripts/render-evidence-chapters.mjs`** composes a full-screen card before each step, using the manifest's step timestamps and statuses. Cards are *inserted between segments* rather than overlaid, so no recorded frame is hidden.
- The skill documents `--build` for targeting an installed Insiders, and the chaptering command.

Rendering is non-fatal: without `ffmpeg`/`ffprobe` it warns and leaves the raw recording untouched.

## Why here rather than in the caller

`microsoft/vscode-engineering` already runs this harness in CI and currently carries its own copy of the renderer, plus two source patches that re-implement what is now supported directly:

| CI patch | Replaced by |
|---|---|
| rewrites `showOverlay` to a no-op | `VSCODE_EVIDENCE_CLEAN_CAPTURE=1` (#331558) |
| injects a video start anchor into `playwrightBrowser.ts` | `videoStartedAt` in the manifest |
| its own `render-video-chapters.mjs` | `test/mcp/scripts/render-evidence-chapters.mjs` |

Those patches only exist because the harness could not do this itself. A follow-up in that repo will delete them and call this script; both local runs and CI then share one implementation.

The Electron path gains an anchor too, which the CI patch never covered — it only patched the browser launcher.

## Validation

- `npm --prefix test/mcp run compile` passes
- rendered a synthetic run end to end with real ffmpeg: output was exactly `60s raw + 3s intro + 2 × 2.5s cards = 68.000s`, and a frame sampled after the first card showed raw footage at the expected offset, confirming alignment
- verified the no-ffmpeg path warns and leaves the recording unchanged

pull_requests.title: Execute a client tool the SDK replays from the transcript
pull_requests.author: RyanEwen
pull_requests.body:
Companion to microsoft/vscode#330730; together they close the remaining ways a client tool call wedges a Claude session in a remote window (microsoft/vscode#322990).

## The failure

Cancel a turn while a client tool call is pending and the transcript keeps an assistant `tool_use` with no `tool_result`. On the next message the SDK resumes and **replays** that call: it invokes the in-process MCP tool directly, without re-streaming the assistant message. The stream mapper — the sole trigger for client-tool execution — sees nothing, so no execution is ever requested. The SDK waits forever, emitting only `tool_progress` heartbeats, and the UI sits at "Considering".

Worse, the dangling `tool_use` is durable: **every** subsequent resume replays it, so the session is permanently wedged. Observed live on 1.133.0:

```
transcript tail:  assistant  tool_use: mcp__client__openBrowserPage (toolu_01Kx9CBY…)   ← no result
21:22:49  chat/turnStarted            ← resume
          (no stream events, no toolCallStart — nothing on the wire)
21:23:10  tool_progress toolu_01Kx9CBY…-heartbeat-0
21:23:39  tool_progress …-heartbeat-1   (forever)
```

## The fix

The MCP handler already receives everything needed — the tool name, the args, and the `tool_use_id`. It now parks via `PendingRequestRegistry.registerAndFire`, firing a `client_tool_invoked` signal. The host checks turn state:

- The call streamed normally → it has protocol state and a client already executing it → the signal is a no-op.
- The call is absent (replay) → the host synthesizes the `ChatToolCallStart` / `ChatToolCallReady` pair the stream would have produced, which drives the existing `ToolClientExecution` request path, so the client executes it like any other call.

`registerAndFire` collects a result buffered before registration *without* firing, so this composes with #330730's eager-execution buffering rather than re-triggering execution.

The synthesis is deliberately host-side (`agentSideEffects`), where turn state lives — the reducer appends blindly on `ChatToolCallStart`, so the session cannot safely emit unconditionally.

## Testing

- `an SDK client tool invocation fires client_tool_invoked and resolves on completion` — session-level, through the real MCP handler wiring.
- `client_tool_invoked synthesizes execution for a replayed call and leaves a streamed one alone` — host-level: the replayed call gains a `Running` tool call with the owning client's contributor and a `ToolClientExecution` request; a second signal for the same id does not duplicate state.
- `handler forwards the tool name and args to awaitResult` — factory-level.
- Suites: AgentSideEffects 220 passing, ClaudeAgent 266 passing / 3 failing (same 3 on an unmodified checkout — model catalog / credential tests, unrelated), buildClientToolMcpServer 6 passing.
- `npm run typecheck-client` clean.

pull_requests.title: agentHost: report completed model calls per turn
pull_requests.author: amunger
pull_requests.body:
https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog/issues/8738

## Overview

### What

Adds `modelCallCount` to the existing per-turn `agentHost.turnCompleted` telemetry event. The measurement reports completed upstream model-response rounds attributed directly to the turn, including responses that request tools and the final tool-free response.

Before this change, equivalent turn-depth analysis was available only for a subset of Copilot turns through `toolCallDetails.numRequests`. After this change, the turn event carries the rollup across Copilot, Claude, and Codex, including turns without tool details.

Provider-native completion boundaries remain intact:

- Copilot uses the response's `apiCallId`, with stable request/message fallbacks, and collapses split assistant messages from one API call.
- Claude uses completed canonical assistant messages and excludes aborted streams.
- Codex uses cumulative per-response token-usage snapshots, retaining a session baseline so replayed and rate-limit-only updates do not increment the count.

The host routes model-call signals through the existing active-turn and subagent mapping, then deduplicates provider call identities in `AgentHostTurnTracker` before emitting the final count.

### Why

Turn-level model-call depth helps identify expensive or looping turns and correlate them with latency, failures, interaction modes, model selection, and subagent use. Keeping the rollup on `agentHost.turnCompleted` avoids a Copilot-only tool-event join and gives the same analysis across Agent Host providers.

## Property-by-property parity

No properties are added or changed.

## Measurement-by-measurement parity

| Measurement | Source | Parity |
|---|---|---|
| `modelCallCount` | Deduplicated completed response boundaries from Copilot `assistant.message`, Claude canonical assistant messages, and Codex per-response usage updates | ✅ Same completed model-response-round signal across providers |

Failed provider attempts that never complete a response are deliberately excluded. Existing per-call response telemetry remains the source for attempt-level reliability analysis.

## Row-count and dashboard implications

- Event cadence remains one `agentHost.turnCompleted` row per tracked turn.
- New rows carry a numeric count, including `0` when no completed response was observed.
- Historical rows have no `modelCallCount`; queries must not treat missing historical values as zero.
- Main-agent and subagent calls are attributed to their own turn rows.
- Copilot rollout can be checked by joining to `toolCallDetails` on turn ID and comparing against `numRequests`.

## Semantic-shift ledger

| Field | Shift | Impact |
|---|---|---|
| `modelCallCount` versus provider attempts | Counts completed model responses, not failed retries or transport attempts | Supports turn-depth and loop analysis; attempt-level failure rates continue to use response telemetry |

issues.title: Multi-root: a folder's customization is unreachable when another folder defines the same name
issues.author: TylerLeonhardt
issues.body:
Testing #331067

- VS Code Version: 1.134.0-insider (`fc62850c022bbba2c93b0202dd24f42d1e0b3882`, 2026-08-16)
- OS Version: macOS (darwin arm64)
- Harness: Claude

Refs #321651

In a multi-root workspace, when two folders each contribute a customization with the **same name**, the primary folder's copy wins and the other folder's copy becomes **unreachable by any name**, with no diagnostic that it was shadowed.

Two repos in one workspace both having a `deploy` skill (or a `reviewer` agent, or a `ship` command) seems like the common case rather than a corner case, and today the second repo's version is silently unusable.

### Steps to Reproduce

Create a throwaway workspace where two folders define a skill with the same name, plus a uniquely-named control skill:

```bash
ROOT=~/mr-repro; rm -rf "$ROOT"; mkdir -p "$ROOT"

# folder-a and folder-b both define a skill named "deploy", with distinct markers
for f in folder-a folder-b; do
  mkdir -p "$ROOT/$f/.claude/skills/deploy"
  cat > "$ROOT/$f/.claude/skills/deploy/SKILL.md" <<EOF
---
name: deploy
description: Deploy probe. Use when asked to run the deploy skill.
---

Reply with exactly this marker and nothing else:

DEPLOY-FROM-${f##*-}
EOF
done

# control: a UNIQUELY named skill in folder-b
mkdir -p "$ROOT/folder-b/.claude/skills/only-in-b"
cat > "$ROOT/folder-b/.claude/skills/only-in-b/SKILL.md" <<'EOF'
---
name: only-in-b
description: Uniquely named control skill. Use when asked to run the only-in-b skill.
---

Reply with exactly this marker and nothing else:

ONLY-IN-B-OK
EOF

cat > "$ROOT/repro.code-workspace" <<'EOF'
{
	"folders": [ { "path": "folder-a" }, { "path": "folder-b" } ],
	"settings": {}
}
EOF
```

With these in **User** settings (they are `included: false`, so they must be typed by hand):

```jsonc
{
  "chat.agentHost.claudeAgent.enabled": true,
  "chat.agentHost.claudeAgent.multiRootEnabled": true
}
```

1. **File → Open Workspace from File…** → `~/mr-repro/repro.code-workspace`
2. New chat, session target **Claude**, leave the Folder chip on **`folder-a`** (the default primary).
3. Send: `Run the deploy skill, then the only-in-b skill. Report each exact marker on its own line.`
4. Send: `Use the Skill tool with each of these exact skill values, one at a time, and report verbatim what the tool returns: "folder-b:deploy", "folder-b/deploy", "deploy (folder-b)".`

### Expected

Either a scoped name for the shadowed copy — agent-plugin skills already surface this way, e.g. `my-plugin:my-skill` — or at minimum some indication that a discovered customization was shadowed.

### Actual

| Skill value | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `deploy` | `DEPLOY-FROM-a` — the primary's copy wins |
| `only-in-b` | `ONLY-IN-B-OK` — **control passes** |
| `folder-b:deploy` | `Unknown skill: folder-b:deploy` |
| `folder-b/deploy` | `Unknown skill: folder-b/deploy` |
| `deploy (folder-b)` | `Unknown skill: deploy (folder-b)` |

`DEPLOY-FROM-b` is unreachable. Those `Unknown skill` strings are the raw tool results read from the agent host trace log, not the model's summary.

**The control is the important part:** `only-in-b` resolves fine, so `folder-b`'s customizations *are* being discovered and invoked. This is specifically collision handling, not a discovery failure. The registry exposes `deploy` exactly once, unprefixed.

Same behavior for a colliding **custom agent** (two folders each defining an agent with the same name).

### Notes

Shadowing itself looks deliberate — `claudeAgentSkillScan.ts`:

```ts
/**
 * Merges parsed components into a name→component map. First-seen wins, so
 * scanning project before user (and skills before commands) makes the
 * earlier entry shadow same-named later ones deterministically.
 */
function collectByName<T extends INamedPluginResource>(into: Map<string, T>, items: readonly T[]): void {
	for (const item of items) {
		if (!into.has(item.name)) { into.set(item.name, item); }
	}
}
```

That reads as written for project-vs-user precedence. The multi-root consequence looks like a side effect rather than an intent — so filing this as a **design gap** rather than a straight bug.

Worth noting `mapDiscoveredCustomizations` already buckets customizations per working directory, so the folder attribution needed to disambiguate is available at that point; the name is collapsed anyway, and the SDK's `Unknown skill` is the downstream symptom.

`collectByName` is unchanged on `main` as of 2026-08-18 (last touched by #328207), so this should still reproduce there — though I verified on `fc62850c022`, not on a `main` build.

**Not verified for Copilot or Codex**, whose customization scans are separate. That comparison would show how broad any fix needs to be; I can run it as part of the Codex pass for #331067.

issues.title: Identical images from different tool calls are shown twice in chat
issues.author: dmitrivMS
issues.body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Open VS Code Insiders and open any folder.
2. Open Chat in Agent mode.
3. Send this prompt:

   ```text
   Using run_in_terminal, download https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0919f3e1-c9e6-47bd-90e3-6dc9f4c4aa24 to a local .png file and print its absolute path. Then use view_image to inspect that exact file. Use both tools and do not skip either one.
   ```

4. Approve the tool calls if prompted and wait for both to finish.
5. Observe the image attachments rendered with the completed tool calls.

### Expected

The identical image is shown once.

### Actual

Two identical image entries are shown: one contributed when the terminal result recognizes the printed local image path, and another contributed by `view_image`.

### Investigation notes

Each tool invocation creates a distinct `vscode-chat-response-resource` URI containing its `toolCallId`, even when two tool results contain byte-identical image data. `ChatThinkingExternalResourceWidget` aggregates image parts from all tool calls, so treating these distinct URIs as distinct resources renders the same image twice.

The aggregation path should suppress image parts with the same MIME type and byte content while preserving genuinely different images.

### Version

- VS Code Insiders 1.134.0-insider
- Commit: `42b1420914c8b46f690e8b5f385722320d7b2d8f`
- OS: Windows x64

issues.title: Agent host: a replayed client tool from a subagent is handled on the parent chat after a restart
issues.author: RyanEwen
issues.body:
### Summary

A client tool that first ran inside a subagent, and is later replayed by the SDK after VS Code restarts, is handled on the parent chat rather than the subagent chat that owns it. It executes and the turn completes, so this is a grouping defect rather than a hang, but the call appears in the wrong conversation and the parent gains a synthesized duplicate.

The in-process half of this is fixed in #330746. This issue is only the after-restart half, which needs coordinated changes and seemed worth raising as one design question rather than patching.

### Why the parent cannot be resolved

The SDK gives the host nothing to resolve it with. The MCP invocation carries only the tool_use id: `extractToolUseId` reads `extra._meta['claudecode/toolUseId']`, and the CLI has the agent id in scope at that dispatch site and deliberately does not include it. The two channels that do carry subagent identity, `canUseTool`'s `agentID` and `parent_tool_use_id` on streamed envelopes, are both unavailable here: a replayed call streams nothing, and inner subagent tools run under `bypassPermissions` so `canUseTool` is skipped.

The host's own inner-to-parent edge (`SubagentRegistry._innerToParent`) is written only by the stream mapper, so it does not exist for a replayed call. `primeFromTranscript` cannot supply it either: it only records `(toolCallId, agentId)` spawn pairs, and it is fed the main transcript, which excludes sidechain entries. Inner calls live in the per-subagent transcripts.

### Why the obvious fix is harmful

Resolving the parent at invoke time, by keeping the registry edge alive past `drainForegroundSpawns` or priming it from elsewhere, is the smaller change and is worse. It sets `parentToolCallId` in cases where the host has no subagent chat, and the signal is then buffered in `_pendingSubagentSignals` awaiting a `subagent_started` that cannot arrive, since that is emitted only from a live inner stream. The parked MCP handler never settles.

The present coupling is safe by accident: the edge exists only when the same code path already emitted `subagent_started`. Any parent resolution from a non-stream source breaks that invariant, which is why #330746 fixes the in-process case with a host-side routing fallback instead.

### What closing the restart case would take

Three coordinated changes, plus one structural wrinkle:

1. **Prime the edge from the SDK's store.** The mapping is persisted as `subagents/agent-<id>.meta.json` -> `toolUseId`, reachable through `listSubagents` and `getSubagentMessages`, whose envelopes carry `parent_tool_use_id`.
2. **Restore a subagent chat for a dangling `Task`.** `_registerRestoredSubagentSummaries` discovers subagents from `ToolResultSubagentContent` gated on `Completed || Running`. The replay case is exactly a `Task` that never completed, which replays as cancelled with no content, so it is skipped.
3. **Populate the routing map.** `_subagentChats` is written only from a live `subagent_started`; no restore path writes it, so routing has nowhere to go even once the chat exists.

The wrinkle: (1) is an async SDK read on a path that is synchronous today.

Shipping only part of this is worse than shipping none. (1) without (2) and (3) is precisely the harmful shape above.

### Offer

I am happy to implement this if it is wanted, and equally happy for it to be closed or reshaped. I have no attachment to the approach above; it is the shape the code suggested to me, not a proposal I am invested in. The reason I am offering rather than just filing is that I want the in-process fix locally today regardless, so the analysis already exists and offering it publicly costs nothing.

If the answer is that client tool execution should be restructured around the SDK invocation instead, as discussed in #330899, this becomes moot and I would rather not build it.

### Environment

Reproduced against a dev container (remote agent host) on `1.133.x`, using the Claude provider.

Related: #330746 (in-process fix), #330899 (root cause of the wider client-tool execution seam).

- The key mcp (or mcp.servers) appears grayed out.
- Hover shows “Unknown Configuration Setting.”
- No intellisense or schema support for entries under that key in the workspace settings context.

**Related Issues / Context:**

- Issue #255220 reports “Unknown Configuration Setting” when configuring mcp.servers in remote user settings. 
- Issue #244525 describes supporting MCP servers in multiple configuration locations including .code-workspace .mcp section.
- No issue explicitly focuses on the workspace-settings / .code-workspace scenario with the UI marking it unknown.

issues.title: `cancelSelection` interferes with extension API `registerCommand("type")`
issues.author: bmalehorn
issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- 🕮 Read our guide about submitting issues: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Submitting-Bugs-and-Suggestions -->
<!-- 🔎 Search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->
<!-- 🧪 Test using the latest Insiders build to see if your issue has already been fixed: https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders/ -->
<!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. -->
<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: No, it's a bug with the extension API itself

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code Version: 1.135.0-insider (Universal)
- OS Version: Darwin arm64 25.4.0

Hello, I'm reporting a bug I've noticed where calling `cancelSelection` interferes with extensions that register the `"type"` command. Normally extensions can register `"type"` to intercept all inputs:

```
subscription = vscode.commands.registerCommand("type", onType)
```

This is useful for Vim-style extensions which want to override regular typed letters like "a", "b", "c". Typing those letters are instead intercepted by the `onType` listener, and don't actually type letters.

However, I noticed that when I trigger a `"cancelSelection"` command, the next typed letter will actually get typed, somehow bypassing the `"type"` register command:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b48758c2-b450-4fd1-9acd-7e2bcd05337e

In the above recording I have a `"type"` command registered, configured so that typing the letter "a" will trigger the `"cancelSelection"` command, and typing the letter "j" will trigger the `"cursorDown"` command.

When I press "j" I would expect the cursor to move down one row.

Instead, when I press "j" it removes most of the section I had previously highlighted, only keeping a couple letters. Then it adds "jj".

Some extra information:
* This issue began occurring sometime between 2026-01-01 and 2026-04-23 on stable
* My extension I used to reproduce this (`bmalehorn.vimspired`) hasn't been updated in 3 years, so it's not a change in the extension. You can view the extension source [here](https://github.com/bmalehorn/vscode-vimspired/blob/578eeb3b80979ac87d33799b8485475503f910b4/src/extension.ts)
* It's possible this is a regression in the extension API, and I'd be fine with a workaround my extension can use
* Canceling selection by pressing Escape does not reproduce the issue (so, what's the difference between Escape and `cancelSelection`?)
* This doesn't occur on reverse selection (selecting from right to left)
* This doesn't occur on multiline selections
* The amount of text remaining (above, only 1 character remained) is not consistently 1 character, it's a variable amount between 0 and the whole line
* Different keys (a, j) and different commands (cursorDown) still reproduce the issue


Steps to Reproduce:

1. Install the extension `bmalehorn.vimspired`
2. Set your vscode config to:
```json
{
  "vimspired.keybindings": {
    "a": "cancelSelection",
    "j": "cursorDown",
  },
}
```
3. in a file, highlight one line from left to right
4. press "a"
5. press "j"

Expected: the cursor moves down 1 row, no text is modified.
Actual: the previously-highlighted portion is partially deleted and "jj" is added to the end.

issues.title: Feature request: React-Grab-like customizable element-selection context for the integrated browser
issues.author: arniebradfo
issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->

I’d like to propose a feature for the integrated browser that lets a repo or page provide custom context when a user selects an element and chooses “Add Element to Chat”.

In short, it would enable [react-grab](https://www.react-grab.com/) like functionality through a hook with the code defined in repo. There are a lot of "grab" libraries designed for different web frameworks: [react](https://www.react-grab.com), [angular](https://angular-grab.com/), [svelte](https://meshkore.com/agent/heicg-svelte-grab), [solidjs](https://github.com/omniaura/solid-grab), [vue](https://vue-grab.vercel.app/), etc... This feature would enable these tools to work inside the integrated browser directly. Each framework would have its own npm package to enable the hook on the browser side.

Today, the flow in `browserEditorChatFeatures.ts` builds a standardized snippet from the selected DOM element (HTML, path, dimensions, computed styles, etc.) and sends that into chat. That is useful, but it is not flexible enough for repos with specialized needs.

As a frontend developer, I want to be able to customize the text snippet that gets attached to chat so I can provide richer, repo-specific context to agents. This should make agent-driven edits more accurate and reduce the need for manual follow-up.

Example use case:
- In a React repo, I want the browser selection flow to call custom code that inspects the React virtual DOM / component tree and returns a structured component-context summary.
- I also want to customize CSS output, for example to de-transform CSS module class names before they are attached to chat, or to remove hashed griffel class names.

Proposal:
- When an element is selected in the integrated browser, VS Code should attempt to invoke a page-provided hook that can customize the context payload.
- The hook should be available for both:
  - the manual “Add Element to Chat” flow from the integrated browser UI, and
  - the browser-tool / agent-driven selection path, so the same repo-specific context can be provided regardless of how the selection was triggered.
- The hook could be exposed as an optional global function on the page, for example:
  - `window.__vscodeIntegratedBrowserGetContext?.(elementData)`
- The hook should be able to return either:
  - a string snippet to append to the existing context, or
  - a richer structured payload that VS Code can render into the chat attachment.
- If the hook is not provided, the current built-in behavior remains unchanged.
- For discoverability, we could add a small docs/help entry or info popover near the element-selection button in the integrated browser UI.

Why this is valuable:
- Different repos need different context
- Frontend teams often want framework-specific summaries
- Better context should lead to better agent suggestions and edits

Possible follow-up work:
- Support repo-specific injection via a script already loaded in the page
- Provide a documented API shape and examples
- Add a UI hint/docs link near the selection action
- Add some default formatters for common libraries like react

---

You can contact me directly on Teams at my Microsoft alias

issues.title: Agent Host chat input reverts while typing after draft sync rejection
issues.author: roblourens
issues.body:
## Problem

Text typed into the chat input for an Agent Host session can repeatedly disappear, leaving the input reverted to an earlier prefix. In the reported case, the input kept returning to `I want to ` as additional words were typed.

The Agent Host protocol logs show this sequence:

1. `I want to ` was the last server-confirmed `chat/draftChanged` value.
2. The UI remained open and editable after the host considered the backing session explicitly deleted.
3. Each longer draft was sent optimistically through `chat/draftChanged`.
4. The host rejected each action with `Session was explicitly deleted`.
5. Subscription state returned to the last confirmed draft, and that state was reflected back into the live chat input.

As a result, every newly typed suffix disappeared shortly after draft synchronization ran. The same state transition can also occur when reconnect processing replaces optimistic state with a fresh server snapshot.

## Expected

Failure to synchronize a draft should not destroy text currently being edited locally.

## Actual

A protocol rollback or snapshot can be interpreted as an incoming draft update and overwrite the live editor contents. This can make the input appear impossible to type into while the underlying session remains stale or unavailable.

(Written by Copilot)
